title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the continuation of La Longue Marche, Grothendieck studies a discrete group Π_0. It is most likely a Teichmüller/mapping-class-type group, and SL(2,Z) is named explicitly on the next page. Π_0 is embedded via a canonical map can: Π_0 → Π(Z) into the Z-points of an integral group-scheme envelope Π over S_0 = Spec Z. The "genres" K_i are conjugacy classes of homomorphisms T_0 ≅ Z → Π_0, plausibly Dehn twists along loops of type i. Over Q each K_i is assumed to extend to an additive one-parameter subgroup k_{i,Q}: G_{a,Q} → Π_Q with image L_{i,Q}.

Previous page: he tries to build integral models of L_{i,Q}. He uses smooth quotients Z_{i,n} of End(L̃_{i,0}), fitting into extensions 1 → nT_0 → Z_{i,n} → (H_{i,n})_{S_0} → 1. He notes that the map Z_{i,n} → Π restricted to nT_0 is generally not a monomorphism. The favourable case is when some nT_0 → Π is a mono (53). That would mean the schematic closure of L_{i,Q} in Π is a smooth subgroup scheme.

This page: he conjectures the condition is also sufficient, at least if one demands that the schematic closure have neutral component isomorphic to G_{a,S_0}. One then gets a homomorphism K_i': G_{a,Z} → Π (54), a closed immersion, unique up to conjugation. Its generic fibre is k_{i,Q} ∘ (r_i·id) for a suitable r_i ∈ Q*+. This is because Aut(G_{a,Q}) = Q* and Aut(G_{a,Z}) = ±1, so the integral structure fixes the scalar up to sign, normalised by r_i > 0.

He is unsure whether the induced map on Z-points, Z ≅ G_a(Z) → Π(Z), factors through can: Π_0 → Π(Z) (55). Such a factorisation would give a homomorphism Z → Π_0 lying in the genre K_i, for instance a primitive 'root' of the twist. A priori the generator of the integral G_a could be a Z-point of Π not coming from Π_0, e.g. when r_i = 1/m. He nevertheless adopts this factorisation as a supplementary hypothesis whenever the K_i' exist. He then announces further 'bonnes hypothèses' realised by working with 'integral' Lie algebras over Spec Z.

Next page: the Lie maps Lie(k_i^!): Z → ΓLie(Π) are assumed to be universal monomorphisms. Hence ΓLie(Π) is generated as a Z-module by the images of the generator and their Π_0-conjugates. The margin calls this hypothesis unreasonable already for Π_0 = SL(2,Z), 'but one can do nothing about it'.

Goal: construct a Z-form of the pro-algebraic (Malcev/relative-type) envelope of a Teichmüller-type group. The Z-form should be pinned down by the Dehn-twist one-parameter subgroups, with a Z-lattice in its Lie algebra spanned by twist logarithms.
errors: The sufficiency claim ('cette condition doit être aussi suffisante') is only conjectured, not proved. In particular, it needs the closure to have connected (or at least G_a-isomorphic) neutral component, which Grothendieck himself adds as an extra requirement.
The sign: G_{a,Z} has automorphism ±1, so 'unique up to conjugation' only holds after normalising r_i > 0. Grothendieck does this implicitly.

The factorisation (55) through Π_0 is explicitly flagged as uncertain and taken as a hypothesis, so it is not an error. However it can fail if Π(Z) contains roots of twist elements that are not in Π_0.

Marginal remark on the next page: for the naive Z-form SL_2 of SL(2,Z), the SL(2,Z)-conjugates of e = (0 1; 0 0) do span sl_2(Z), since g e g^{-1} = [[-ab, a²], [-b², ab]] gives e, -f and e - f - h. So the 'unreasonableness' must come from the full envelope Π of the virtually free group SL(2,Z), which is much larger than SL_2, or from a stronger consequence stated later. It does not come from SL_2 itself.

ideas.what: Integral (Spec Z) model of the algebraic envelope of a discrete group, with Dehn-twist-type elements giving additive one-parameter subgroups whose schematic closures should be smooth with neutral component G_{a,Z}.
ideas.modern_name: Integral forms / Z-structures on Malcev or relative completions of mapping class groups; unipotent one-parameter subgroups via logarithms of Dehn twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malcev; Deligne; Hain (relative completion of mapping class groups, 1997). Integral structures much less systematically studied.
ideas.where_published: Unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche (cote 140-4). Esquisse d'un programme mentions Teichmüller tower and discrete groups but not this construction.

ideas.what: Rescaling ambiguity: a Q-isomorphism G_a → L_Q extends to Z only after composing with r_i·id, r_i ∈ Q*+. This raises the question whether the integral generator lies in Π_0 (a 'root' of the twist in the same genre).
ideas.modern_name: Integral normalisation of one-parameter subgroups / roots of Dehn twists

ideas.what: Hypothesis (next page) that the Z-Lie algebra of the envelope is spanned by Π_0-conjugates of the generators of the twist subgroups.
ideas.modern_name: Lie lattice generated by logarithms of Dehn twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related ideas in Hain, and in work on Lie algebras of mapping class groups (Morita, Oda, Nakamura), but rationally, not integrally.

missed.claim: A programme to give the algebraic envelope of Teichmüller-type groups a canonical Z-structure. Dehn-twist genres would determine smooth G_{a,Z}-subgroups, and their generators would be required to come from the discrete group itself. Integral models of relative/Malcev completions of mapping class groups have received little attention compared with rational and pro-ℓ versions.
missed.quote: On trouve alors, en tout cas, un homomorphisme unique (à conjugaison près) K_i' : T_0 ↪ Π tel que K'_{iQ} soit de la forme K_{iQ}∘(r_i id)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral/arithmetic structures on completions of mapping class groups bear on questions about congruence quotients and integral Lie algebras of twists. Grothendieck's explicit criterion — schematic closure smooth with neutral component G_a — is a concrete test one could run on known examples such as braid groups and genus 0/1 mapping class groups.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a notable unpublished glimpse of Grothendieck trying to put Z-structures on envelopes of Teichmüller groups via Dehn-twist one-parameter subgroups. However, it is tentative, hypothesis-laden and self-doubting (he finds it unreasonable for SL(2,Z)), with no finished result.
transcription_corrections: 'ait une comp.[?] montre[?] qui soit = isom. : Gr.-So.[?]' should read roughly 'ait une comp. neutre qui soit ≃ G_{a,S_0}' (neutral component isomorphic to G_a over S_0 = Spec Z).
In (54) the symbol is underlined k_i' (a homomorphism of group schemes from underlined T_0 to underlined Π), not a double-underlined K.
'Je vais néanmoins la poser comme hypothèse suppl.' is correct; the inserted word is 'suppl.' (supplémentaire).
